segments.text: Jarvis one point twelve is here — a big usability round for the alert view. Let's walk through what's new.
The filters you use every day now live in the toolbar. Pick one, and the matcher chips are applied instantly.
Star the one you start your day with. Open Jarvis without a filter in the link, and it is applied for you. Unstar it, and you are back to every alert.
A card carries a lot of labels, and only a few of them tell you which alert this is. Pin those, and they move to the front of every card — in a color you choose.
The rest can be hidden. A hidden label still filters and still shows in the detail panel, it just stops competing for space on your cards.
Back on the cards, your pinned label comes first. Hidden labels sit behind a plus chip and open in a popover, so nothing jumps around.
Grouping moved out of the settings and into the toolbar. Every label is there, searchable, with the number of alerts behind it.
Pick one, and the board regroups. Here, one section per cluster.
Cards now flow into columns balanced by their real height, and the most recently fired group comes first.
If you prefer a fixed layout, the new card columns slider pins the count on every screen.
The header got quieter. Cluster health, refresh and info open on hover, right under the bar.
And settings, theme and your account all live in one user menu, always in the same place.
Open an alert, and claiming it is a single click in the detail panel. No form, no dialog — your team sees the owner right away.
If you want to say what you are doing, add a short note afterwards. It shows up right on the card, where your team is looking anyway.
Three more things: filter links now use Alertmanager's own matcher syntax, your settings follow your account across devices, and the cards themselves got a lot calmer.
Under the hood, this release fixes a batch of history issues, most of them for PostgreSQL setups with several replicas.
Jarvis is free and open source. Find it on GitHub, at k j one eight seven slash jarvis.
